Paresh Nath Mondal & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors
on 16 March, 2023
Author: Shampa Sarkar

Bench: Shampa Sarkar
 16.03.2023
Court No. 19
Item no.29
 Cp
 W.P.A. No. 3447 of 2023
 Paresh Nath Mondal & anr.
 Vs.
 The State of West Bengal & Ors.
 Mr. Samim Ahammed
 Ms. Saloni Bhattacharjee
 Ms. Ambiya Khatun
 ....for the petitioners.

Mr. Partha Pratim Roy
 Mr. Ram Chandra Guchhait
 ....for the State.
The admitted position is that a part of the land  of the petitioners had been used by the erstwhile  pradhan of Dabuk Gram Panchayat for construction  of a village road.

It appears that the panchayat  authorities even in 2021 had accepted the above fact  and had intimated the Block Development Officer  that the land had been taken from the petitioner no.
 1 on the assurance that the petitioner no. 2 would be  given a job.
 The petitioners submit that if no employment  could be given by the authorities, the authorities Paresh Nath Mondal & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 16 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102010388/
1  ought to at least pay some compensation or  consideration for the land which was used sometime  in 2016, by the gram panchayat.

sentences.text: 2  Mr. Guchhait, learned advocate for the State respondents opposes the contention of the petitioners and submits that the petitioner no. 1 had voluntarily allowed the construction of the road through the land.
The panchayat authorities were not authorized to promise a job to the petitioner no. 2.
According to him, the writ petition is an afterthought and should be dismissed without any orders.
For the purpose of determination of the issue, Section 44 of the West Bengal Panchayat Act, 1973 is required to be considered.

The same is quoted below:
"44. Acquisition of land for Gram Panchayat.

- Where a Gram Panchayat requires land for carrying out any of the purposes of this Act, it may negotiate with the person or persons having interest in the said land, and if it fails to reach an agreement, it may make an application to the Collector for the acquisition of the land, who may, if he is satisfied that the land is required for a pubic purpose, take steps to acquire the land and such land shall, on acquisition, vest in the Gram Panchayat."

The expression 'negotiation' mentioned in Section 44 of the said Act means an attempt to obtain a 'no objection' or voluntary handing over of the land in favour of the authority, without any condition.

If owners of the land proposed to be used by the panchayat authorities do not of their own accord, allow or permit user of the land, the only option left to the authority for user of such land would be to initiate proceedings for acquisition of the same.
The policy of the government to engage or appoint a member of the family of the land loser is not foreign to this State.

Thus, when the panchayat authorities had indicated that the land was taken only on the assurance that the petitioner no. 2 would be given a job, the negotiation as contemplated in Section 44 had not taken place.
In the alternative, the result of such negotiation was that a member of the family of the land loser would be given a job.
Thus, this is not a case of voluntary handing over of the land to the panchayat authorities.

A poor and uneducated man from a rural area may not be conversant with the finer nuances of law,
and on the assurance of a job may have handed over a portion of his land for the village road.

Under such circumstances, the District Magistrate, Birbhum shall cause an inspection through the Sub-Divisional Officer, Rampurhat and the Block Development Officer, Mayuershwar - I Paresh Nath Mondal & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 16 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102010388/
2

sentences.text:
Development Block in the presence of the petitioners and the authorities of Dabuk Gram Panchayat,
in order to determine the extent of land which was exclusively owned and possessed by the petitioners, but had been utilized for the road.
Upon such inspection, a report shall be prepared.
If it is found that the allegation was correct, in that event a proposal shall be filed before the court as to how the petitioners may be compensated.
Whether consideration at the market rate prevalent at the time of the construction of the road shall be paid or any other form of acquisition shall be initiated, shall be mentioned in the report.
It is expected that the report and the proposal of the government shall be before this court on May 16, 2023, when the matter will appear in the supplementary list as a New Motion.

(Shampa Sarkar, J.)
